# Masked V2V Code Map — AST Jump Index & `cannot_see` Boundaries

<!-- Generated by `bench/masked_code_map.py --write`. Do not edit by hand; run `bench/masked_code_map.py --write`. -->

Companion to [`docs/research/masking/2026-10-26_code_map_and_simplification_plan.md`](../research/masking/2026-10-26_code_map_and_simplification_plan.md),
[`docs/masked_v2v/code_map_stages.md`](code_map_stages.md) (Part 1), and
[`docs/masked_v2v/code_map_contracts.md`](code_map_contracts.md) (Parts 2 & 4).

## How a Dedicated Gemini / AGY Session Refreshes the Code Map (Anti-Drift Runbook)

1. **Detect AST Function Drift (`< 0.1s`)**:
   Run `$H3_PYTHON bench/masked_code_map.py --drift` (where `$H3_PYTHON` is the ComfyUI venv Python).
   It hashes every function's AST body (ignoring line-number shifts caused by edits higher in the file) and prints:
   - Every `file::symbol` whose AST body changed, with its **new** `StartLine-EndLine` coordinates for `read_file`.
   - Every `### Stage X.Y` or `### Section 2x` block in `code_map_stages.md` / `code_map_contracts.md` that cites a changed symbol.
2. **Targeted Read & Narrative Edit (`1-3s` per stage)**:
   Call `read_file` on just the reported `StartLine-EndLine` of each changed function and update only the flagged
   `### Stage` / `### Section` block (`< 15` short bullet lines) in `code_map_stages.md` or `code_map_contracts.md`.
3. **Regenerate Jump Index & Run Gate Checks**:
   Run `$H3_PYTHON bench/masked_code_map.py --write && $H3_PYTHON bench/masked_code_map.py --check`
   followed by `$H3_PYTHON bench/check_doc_links.py docs/masked_v2v/CODE_MAP_INDEX.md docs/masked_v2v/code_map_stages.md docs/masked_v2v/code_map_contracts.md docs/research/masking/2026-10-26_code_map_and_simplification_plan.md`.

## Part 2d — Declared `cannot_see` Boundaries Across All Tools

Extracted from AST constants and record writers so line numbers and strings never drift:

### `bench/capture_masked_run.py::SIZES_CANNOT_SEE` (`L753-L755`) — `sizes` (`part_sizes`)
- whether a small part is a sliver of the part or a whole small face (the class map calls both the part's class): look at a frame; and the size the part is drawn at on a load rendered zoomed in, which is larger than these whole-frame pixels by the zoom, squared (the starting floor is held to it: floor_zoom)

### `bench/capture_masked_run.py::PIECES_CANNOT_SEE` (`L759-L760`) — `pieces=largest` (`largest_piece`)
- whether a piece taken away was the part (a face behind a raised arm or behind hair is rightly in two pieces, and the smaller one is then lost) or something else the class map calls the part: look at a frame it names

### `bench/capture_masked_run.py::OTHER_CANNOT_SEE` (`L4061-L4062`) — `preflight` (`flag_runs` / `flag_segments`)
- whether they are hidden on those frames or the tracker lost them while they are in view; in view, with the load's region reaching them, nothing would keep the region off them

### `bench/capture_masked_run.py::HAIR_IN_HOLE_CANNOT_SEE` (`L5169-L5179`) — `her_hair_in_hole` / `hair-in-hole`
- hair the part model does not label as Hair (a few pixels, behind a brim, in motion blur: on 4912e her crown above the hat on 4944 and 4945 is Background even on the whole frame, run on those two frames on 2026-10-22), so part 3 cannot find it and only part 2 can catch the frames
- with only her own class map (the preview's, of her crop with other people blanked), hair beyond that crop or on a frame where the preview did not read her; the strangers file's whole-frame class map, where its record names one, is read in its place
- her own hair inside her person track and outside her head track and her part: it is hers by SAM and is no unclaimed hair here
- whether her head is in view on a frame SAM lost it: part 2 reads SAM's own score, not the picture, so a frame where her head is hidden and SAM still holds her (her arm in view) is asked about too
- a piece of unclaimed hair under SEGMENT_PX that touches another person: neither added nor asked about, only counted

### `bench/head_tube_parts.py::FACIAL_HAIR_CANNOT_SEE` (`L163-L172`) — `face_piece_kept_whole` (`facial_hair=keep`)
- a hand or arm the part model calls Face_Neck where it touches the face (4912e's raised hand): kept where it lies in the face's columns; what the columns cut is recorded a frame (`cut_by_the_columns_px`); hands and arms labelled as hand/arm classes in the class map (`JAW_BEARD_EXCLUDE_CLASSES`) are excluded from the downward jaw extension (`excluded_hand_arm_px`)
- a beard wider than the face's columns and FACE_COLUMN_PAD_PX (a profile where the face inside the tube is a sliver): cut there, and recorded
- a piece of the part not joined to the face and below JAW_BEARD_PAD_FRAC of the face height: not kept
- where the beard ends: the connected Face_Neck piece is the neck as well as the beard, and the downward jaw extension reaches JAW_BEARD_PAD_FRAC of the face height below each column of the face

### `bench/facts_pass.py::CANNOT_SEE` (`L43-L46`) — `run_facts_pass` (`facts_pass.py`)
- pixel appearance, identity likeness, lip-sync accuracy, temporal flicker, and whether a mouth mode or region boundary looks natural in the rendered video

### `bench/strangers.py::run` (`L625-L650`) — `<preview>_strangers.json["cannot_see"]`
- Record key `cannot_see` (`13` strings): people missed by both whole-frame Sapiens2 (`c == 0`) and SAM 3.1 (`people.npz`) stay regenerable
  (`426638a6` unions unowned SAM detections `who is None` into `people[i]` and `core[i]` where `c == 0`);
  people missed by SAM 3.1 for `> hold_frames` (`8`) whose pieces touch a subject are handed back (`NO_OTHER = "handed_back_on_no_other_person"`);
  stranger components touching a subject with no 18-class `CORE_CLASSES` or unowned SAM detection pixels (`held = piece & core[i]`) are handed back (`NO_CORE = "no body core of its own"`).

### `bench/shot_to_load.py::face_cues` (`L3586-L3589`), `figures_of` (`L3618`) & `bench/measure_blocks.py::measure_luma_blocks`
- `bench/shot_to_load.py:3586-3589` (`cannot_see` on ear/face-score cues in `face_cues`) and `:3618` (`figures_of`).
- `bench/measure_blocks.py:859-861` (`cannot_see` on 16x16 grid block measurements in `measure_luma_blocks`).
